subject: protocol approval
rationale: The protocol declares its own vocabularies DRAFT until a named scientist records an approval against its content hash. No such record exists.

subject: vocabulary status
rationale: Every field definition a curator would work to is draft. A curator working to a draft vocabulary produces drafts.

subject: amitriptyline is one two-gene decision, not two axes
rationale: Whether the first release models amitriptyline as a two-gene matrix, restricts itself to the single-gene cells the source states separately, or removes amitriptyline from the first release.

subject: clopidogrel recommendations depend on indication
rationale: Whether the first release carries an indication axis, restricts itself to one indication and says so, or defers clopidogrel.

subject: the five-phenotype vocabulary does not fit CYP2D6
rationale: Whether the phenotype vocabulary is extended, whether unrepresentable phenotypes are refused explicitly, and whether CYP2D6 carries an activity score.

subject: the FDA does not cover one declared axis
rationale: Whether an axis without regulator labelling may still be released, and how its absence is shown.

subject: the clopidogrel boxed warning no longer says 'poor metabolizer'
rationale: How label extraction is keyed, and how a zero-result extraction is distinguished from a genuine absence.

subject: the 13 unlinked in-scope legacy candidates
rationale: Each names no upstream record. A curator sources evidence for the axis; the legacy row's own wording is not evidence and must not be the starting point.
